html:
The Fante are an Akan people of the central coast of what is now Ghana. The map shows their lands in its 1815 snapshot, when they were in a long struggle with Asante.

The Fante lived in a string of small states, loosely linked around their old centre at Mankessim. Their coast was lined with European forts such as Cape Coast Castle and Elmina, and they grew rich as middlemen, selling gold and slaves to Europeans and European goods inland.

Asante wanted direct access to the coast. It invaded Fante land in 1806 and again in the 1810s, and the British, who depended on the Fante, were drawn into the Anglo-Ashanti wars. In 1868 the Fante states formed the Fante Confederacy and wrote a constitution in 1871, an early attempt at modern African self-rule. Britain broke it up and in 1874 made the coast the Gold Coast Colony.
